title: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
name: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
goal: Keep several explanations alive until new evidence separates them.
steps:
1. Keep the event fixed.
2. Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next.
4. Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy.

title: ADD THE PREFIX
name: ADD THE PREFIX
goal: Notice the thought as mental activity, then keep doing what you chose.
steps:
1. Put “I am noticing my mind produce…” before the thought. Say the whole sentence once at normal speed.
2. Notice what remains true and what loses command authority.
3. Carry on with the next chosen task while the sentence exists nearby.

title: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
name: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
goal: Respect the warning in a thought without letting it sign the contract.
steps:
1. Ask what danger the thought is trying to prevent.
2. Offer a precise thank-you for that intention.
3. Answer: “I’m not signing this instruction.” Choose one action that reflects what matters to you while keeping any useful caution.
4. Respect the alarm; decline the contract.

title: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
name: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
goal: Watch a thought arrive and leave without helping it stay or go.
steps:
1. Place the thought on something imagined as moving: a bus, leaf, or subtitle.
2. Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one fixed visual point.
4. Another carrier may come; none owns the station.
numberedSteps:
1. Place the thought on something imagined as moving: a bus, leaf, or subtitle.
2. Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one fixed visual point.
4. Another carrier may come; none owns the station.
numbered_steps:
1. Place the thought on something imagined as moving: a bus, leaf, or subtitle.
2. Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one fixed visual point.

win: The thought completed one imagined journey while your attention returned to something real.
mindBend: A thought can pass through awareness without needing an exit strategy from you.
mind_bend: A thought can pass through awareness without needing an exit strategy from you.

text_default:
ENTER THE ACTION

PLAY TIME
60–90 seconds

GOAL
Re-enter an ordinary activity through your senses instead of demanding perfect focus.

STEPS
1. Choose one ordinary activity.
2. Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
3. When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself.
4. Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
5. Participation, not perfect focus, is the target.

WIN
Attention wandered and returned through the next physical contact point without self-scolding.

MIND BEND
Focus is not a continuous state — it is repeatedly rebuilt at the moment of return.

FORMULA FLOW
Choose Ordinary → Place Vision → Leave Re → Stay Activity → Enter Fully

PAUSE
Do not narrow attention during driving, caregiving, or tasks requiring broad awareness.

goal: Test whether a tiny believable softening changes the body's defensive setting.
steps:
1. Without forcing happiness, release the forehead, loosen the eyes, and lift the mouth corners by two percent.
2. Keep the expression believable.
3. Hold it while resting your gaze on one neutral visual point.
4. Ask whether defence changed by even half a notch.

title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
name: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
goal: Use a slow movement sequence to prove your body can follow deliberate instructions.
steps:
1. Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and shift your gaze.
2. Do A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Do C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, restart instead of speeding up.
4. Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the code stop.

title: THE FOUR-LETTER BRAKE
name: THE FOUR-LETTER BRAKE
goal: Interrupt momentum long enough to choose the smallest safe move.
steps:
1. Stop every nonessential movement.
2. Take one physical step back.
3. Observe facts, sensations, and the strongest impulse.
4. Proceed with the smallest safe move that will still make sense in an hour.
5. Do not negotiate with momentum between letters.

title: ONE FOOT HERE, EYES OPEN
name: ONE FOOT HERE, EYES OPEN
goal: Re-anchor in the current room without pulling more detail from the past.
steps:
1. Press one foot into the floor and keep both eyes open.
2. Look at each room corner and name one visible difference.
3. Say your current age without describing the earlier event.
4. Move farther from anything that increases the memory alarm.
5. Contact a safe person if present-time orientation stays weak.

2. Look at each room corner and name one visible difference.
3. Say your current age without describing the earlier event.
4. Move farther from anything that increases the memory alarm.
5. Contact a safe person if present-time orientation stays weak.
numbered_steps:

2. Look at each room corner and name one visible difference.
3. Say your current age without describing the earlier event.
4. Move farther from anything that increases the memory alarm.
5. Contact a safe person if present-time orientation stays weak.
win: Your foot, open eyes, current age, and room cues made the present easier to locate.
mindBend: A memory alarm can borrow the body's sense of 'now'. Present facts return a date and place to the signal.

This is grounding only, not trauma treatment.

Give pleasant, unpleasant, dull, and vivid sensations the same brief welcome.

STEPS
1. Let the field choose its next foreground.
2. Pleasant, unpleasant, dull, or vivid—offer each the same brief hospitality.
3. When preference reaches to grip or reject, include that movement too.
4. End by noticing the whole room at once.

WIN
Preference itself became another event in the field instead of deciding what had to stay or leave.

MIND BEND
Gripping and rejecting are extra movements added to sensation — noticing those movements reveals what the raw experience was doing first.

FORMULA FLOW
Let Field → Pleasant → Include Movement → End Whole

SAFETY
PAUSE
Use a stable anchor instead during high body alarm or feeling unreal or disconnected.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: EXPAND–GATHER–EXPAND
name: EXPAND–GATHER–EXPAND
goal: Move from the whole moment to the breath, then back out to wider awareness.
steps:
1. First, acknowledge the full weather of the moment.
2. Next, gather attention around breathing as a small centre.
3. Finally, widen to the whole body and surrounding space.
4. Spend roughly one minute in each shape.
5. Carry the final wide frame into your next movement.

name: RAIN WITHOUT THE UMBRELLA
goal: Acknowledge what is here, meet it kindly, and remember it is not all of you.
steps:
1. Recognise what is here.
2. Allow this moment of it to exist.
3. Investigate with one kind question about body or need.
4. Notice that the experience is present but not the whole of you.
5. Move through R–A–I–N once; resolution is not a required fifth letter.

mind_bend_text: Acceptance is not a fifth step called resolution. Sometimes the shift is simply ending the demand that the experience disappear.
full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
60–90 seconds

GOAL
Acknowledge what is here, meet it kindly, and remember it is not all of you.

STEPS
1. Recognise what is here.
2. Allow this moment of it to exist.
3. Investigate with one kind question about body or need.
4. Notice that the experience is present but not the whole of you.
5. Move through R–A–I–N once; resolution is not a required fifth letter.

WIN
The experience was recognised, allowed, gently investigated, and placed inside a larger sense of self.

MIND BEND
Acceptance is not a fifth step called resolution. Sometimes the shift is simply ending the demand that the experience disappear.

FORMULA FLOW
Recognise → Allow Moment → Question About → Experience → Move R

SAFETY
PAUSE
Skip investigation when acute distress requires grounding first.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LISTEN PAST THE SOUND
name: LISTEN PAST THE SOUND
goal: Follow a sound all the way into silence without keeping it alive in memory.
steps:
1. Ring, play, or notice a safe sustained sound.
2. Follow its decay with precision until you cannot locate any remainder.
3. Stay with the silence that receives it, not with memory of the tone.
4. Let the next surroundings sound end the practice.

title: NOTICE THE NOTICING
name: NOTICE THE NOTICING
goal: Notice a sensation, then notice that knowing is already happening.
steps:

3. Ask, without answering verbally, ‘How is this already known?’ Rest with knowing rather than searching for a separate thing called awareness.
4. Return by naming one visible fact.

title: THE BREATH HINGE
name: THE BREATH HINGE
goal: Feel the natural turning points of breathing without holding them open.
steps:
1. Follow a natural inhale to the instant it turns toward exhale.
2. Do not hold or stretch the hinge.
3. Notice the same effortless change at the bottom of exhalation.
4. Visit each threshold lightly, then allow several breaths to pass unwatched.
numberedSteps:
1. Follow a natural inhale to the instant it turns toward exhale.

3. Notice the same effortless change at the bottom of exhalation.
4. Visit each threshold lightly, then allow several breaths to pass unwatched.

PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Stay with bare seeing or hearing before the mind turns contact into a story.

STEPS

PAUSE

title: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
name: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
ritual_name: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
goal: Put blended feelings back into the order they actually arrived.
steps:
1. Name up to three present feelings. Do not explain them yet.
2. Which arrived first? Put it at the left of a short line.
3. Add the concrete cue that each feeling answered—words heard, an image, a body change, or a later thought.
4. Read the sequence once: ‘First ___ answered ___; then ___ answered ___.’ Stop after the order is clear.

mind_bend_text: Feelings that arrive seconds apart can fuse into one verdict; restoring order shows that they may be answering different events.
full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
60–90 seconds

GOAL
Put blended feelings back into the order they actually arrived.

STEPS
1. Name up to three present feelings. Do not explain them yet.
2. Which arrived first? Put it at the left of a short line.
3. Add the concrete cue that each feeling answered—words heard, an image, a body change, or a later thought.
4. Read the sequence once: ‘First ___ answered ___; then ___ answered ___.’ Stop after the order is clear.

WIN
Each emotion was linked to its own cue, making the sequence clearer without needing a bigger story.

MIND BEND
Feelings that arrive seconds apart can fuse into one verdict; restoring order shows that they may be answering different events.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Mix → Find First → Link Cue → Read Order

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if sequencing pulls you into flashback, self-blame, numbness, or forced certainty about the past.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
name: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
ritual_name: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
goal: Let one thought end without immediately filling the empty beat with another.
steps:
1. Wait for a thought to end naturally.
2. At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
4. Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count the gap only after it is over.

title: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
name: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
goal: Make another thinking lap pay for the time it takes from real life.
steps:
1. Name the exact question you want one more thinking lap to answer. One sentence only.
2. Choose what those three minutes will replace: rest, a message, food, movement, work, or a decision. Say the trade plainly.
3. If the trade is worth it, set three minutes and think only about the named question. If not, close the lap now.
4. When the clock ends, stop without buying another lap. Do the displaced activity or deliberately let it go.
numberedSteps:

title: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
name: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
ritual_name: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
goal: Put one memory segment into past tense while inserting present facts between loaded lines.
steps:

2. After every emotionally loaded sentence, insert three present facts: your present location, the current year, and what choice exists now.
3. Finish with: ‘That ended; this moment is different.’

title: THIRD-PERSON OWNERSHIP TEST
name: THIRD-PERSON OWNERSHIP TEST
goal: Step back from the mind's content without stepping away from the action you own.
steps:
1. Frame the moment once as ‘this mind is predicting…’ or ‘the system is producing…’.
2. Notice what changes in intensity, responsibility, and choice.
3. Then return to first person for the action you really own: ‘I will…’.
4. Distance the content, not agency.

plain_text:
THIRD-PERSON OWNERSHIP TEST

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
Step back from the mind's content without stepping away from the action you own.

STEPS
1. Frame the moment once as ‘this mind is predicting…’ or ‘the system is producing…’.
2. Notice what changes in intensity, responsibility, and choice.
3. Then return to first person for the action you really own: ‘I will…’.
4. Distance the content, not agency.

WIN
The prediction was described at a distance, then first-person agency returned exactly where behaviour began.

MIND BEND
Taking distance from a thought helps only if responsibility stays close; stepping back does not hand your choices away.

FORMULA FLOW
Describe Event → Change → Return Person → Loosen Grammar

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if altered pronouns make you feel more disconnected from yourself.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

name: CALL THE INNER COUNCIL
goal: Let different inner needs speak once, then give coordination to the part protecting the whole system.
steps:

goal: Use a real present-day support voice without imagining the past scene.

4. Decide whether to contact them or return to a neutral task.

goal: Review a relationship as separate events, patterns, context, repair attempts, and outcomes.
steps:

plain:
STOP REHEARSING THE REPLY

PLAY TIME
45–90 seconds

GOAL
Stop composing your reply while the other person is still speaking.

STEPS
1. Park your reply until they finish.
2. Compare the message with the observable facts.
3. Choose one plain opening line.

WIN
The message reached completion, facts could be compared afterward, and only then did one plain opening line form.

MIND BEND
Reply rehearsal steals incoming information. The answer you prepare early may be responding to a sentence the other person never finishes saying.

FORMULA FLOW
Park Rest → Test Match → Say Simply

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if this makes you less steady, more distressed, or less able to act safely. Use human, professional, medical, or emergency support when the situation needs more than self-help.
This brief reset is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.

1. Let the first pressure pass without acting.
2. Slow your body one notch.
3. Separate the event from the meaning you fear.
4. Say how much capacity is genuinely available right now.
5. Choose one steady sentence you can send without hurrying.

WIN
The facts, feared meaning, and available capacity separated before one sendable sentence was chosen.

MIND BEND
A pressured body can make a correct message come out too strongly. Pace is part of good judgement.

FORMULA FLOW
Hold Choice → Cool Pace → Unmix Story → Set Limit → Make Sentence

SAFETY
PAUSE
Do not send, drive, confront, threaten, or act while control feels reduced. Move away from weapons and hazards; use human or emergency support if anyone may be unsafe.
This is brief self-help, not treatment or emergency care.

title: WHO YOU CHOOSE NEXT
name: WHO YOU CHOOSE NEXT
goal: Keep a disturbing thought separate from identity and let the next chosen action represent you instead.
steps:
1. Catch the thought without explaining it.
2. Say, “My mind produced this; it is not my biography.”
3. Name one value you want to stand for in the next minute—kind, honest, patient, careful, brave, or another word that fits.
4. Do one ten-second action that matches that principle.
5. Leave the thought unanswered and continue with the action.
